name: Deep Violet
lede: Deep Violet is a very dark, reddish reading of [[violet]], close enough to near-black that it was also sold as Eggplant Purple.

sections.title: Almost black
sections.body:
The name follows the library's modifier grammar, *deep* plus [[violet]]; our record traces the exact chip to the 2010 xkcd online color survey, a crowd-sourced naming exercise rather than a dictionary or a painted plate [1]. The same hex has also circulated under Eggplant Purple, an alternate commercial name with no further history recorded here [1].

At lightness 16 out of 100 it sits near the dark end of the whole violet family; its closest look-alike on file is [[deep-purple]], about 4.1 units off, with [[petunia]] and [[grape-purple]] a little further out [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This exact shade is almost absent from our archive: a near match appears in just 1 of roughly 23,700 paintings, under 0.01 per cent, as photographed [3]. A color this close to black is hard to tell apart from shadow in a photographed, varnished canvas, which likely suppresses the count further [3]. The single match is a screen comparison only, not a pigment identification [3].
